# VS Code (Copilot Chat)

This host keeps its config in the project folder, so the setup travels with the repo.

## Install

```
headwaters install --host vscode
```

The installer prints the diff first and writes only after a yes; `--dry-run` stops at the
diff and `--json` prints the same plan as a document.

## Files

| File | What the install does |
| --- | --- |
| `<project>/.vscode/mcp.json` | create |
| `<project>/.vscode/settings.json` | create |
| `<appdata>/Code/User/chatLanguageModels.json` | create |
| `<project>/.github/copilot-instructions.md` | create |
| `<project>/.github/prompts/headwaters-auto.prompt.md` | create |
| `<project>/.github/prompts/headwaters-free.prompt.md` | create |
| `<project>/.github/prompts/headwaters-handoff.prompt.md` | create |
| `<project>/.github/prompts/headwaters-local.prompt.md` | create |
| `<project>/.github/prompts/headwaters-status.prompt.md` | create |

## What you still do

- VS Code asks once for the gateway token: paste the daemon's own token from <state>/daemon.token into the "Headwaters" prompt, or set the profile input.
- Business or Enterprise: an admin has to allow "Bring Your Own Language Model Key in VS Code" before a custom endpoint appears; the setting alone is not enough.
- Reload the window after the first install so the MCP server and the models appear.
- Prompt files land in .github/prompts: type /headwaters-<name> in Copilot Chat.

## Templates behind this page

The entries above are rendered from `vscode_mcp`, `vscode_settings`, `vscode_byok` in `headwaters/installer/templates/`, so this page and a real install cannot drift.

## Check it

```
headwaters doctor --host vscode
```

The doctor reads this host's own config back and reports a missing or stale entry; a
clean report means the host is talking to the gateway.

## Remove it

```
headwaters uninstall --host vscode
```

The uninstall restores the backed-up file unless it was edited after the install; then it
asks for `--force`.
